newsitem.title: USA: CalPERS says ADM board proposal gaining favor.
newsitem.headline: CalPERS says ADM board proposal gaining favor.

text.p: A proposal calling for an independent board of directors at Archer Daniels Midland Co has garnered a significant number of votes, the California Public Employees Retirement System (CalPERS) said.

A survey of votes cast thus far indicated that 47 percent are in favor of the proposal, which is co-sponsored by CalPERS and the Florida Retirement System Trust Fund, said Brad Pacheco, a CalPERS spokesman.
He cautioned that a significant number of shares have not yet been voted in advance of ADM's October 17 annual meeting.
"We see some people sitting on the fence," Pacheco said.
CalPERS also said it withheld its estimated 3.5 million shares from election of the ADM director nominees.
CalPERS said its proposal gained support after ADM pleaded guilty to two counts of price fixing and agreed to pay $100 million in fines.

"There is no more important time than now, nor greater need to send the strongest possible signal for meaningful change in ADM's governance," James Burton, CalPERS chief executive officer, said in a statement.
"Quite simply, an independent board is the best way to prevent corporate criminal activity, so that this company will never again have to squander shareholders money to pay criminal fines," he added.
The measure calling for an independent board, consisting of members with no personal or business ties to ADM, is one of three proposals offered by institutional shareholders.
Other measures call for confidential voting for board members when there is no competing proxy and the establishment of personal financial liability for directors in cases of gross negligence.
